correctness.rationale: Every nonzero circle tangent to the two nonparallel limiting lines has center on exactly one normalized angle-bisector branch. On each branch the exact center is affine-linear in the signed distance \(q\). The determinant-pencil discriminant is a necessary tangency condition and is an exact squarefree degree-\(8\) polynomial over \(\mathbf Q(\sqrt{3563201},\sqrt{6112121})\). Exact Sturm counting gives \(8\) real roots on the plus branch and \(6\) on the minus branch, with \(q=0\) excluded. The source independently establishes exactly \(14\) real QL² circles for this configuration, so the necessary-condition root counts are saturated and the branch split is exactly \(8+6\).

value.rationale: The QL² maximum is the unresolved constituent singled out by the initiating paper as the next obstruction to improving the real-circle record. The exact split shows that the record configuration already saturates one entire degree-eight angle-bisector branch and that the missing two real solutions are localized to one conjugate pair on the other branch. This is a natural structural diagnostic for a live real-enumerative optimization problem, not an arbitrary subcount.
